newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT sees approval of rate plan in Sept.
newsitem.headline: PLDT sees approval of rate plan in Sept.

text.p: The Philippine Long Distance Co said on Monday it expects the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) to approve its proposed rate scheme by next month.
"We expect the NTC to hand down a favourable decision by September, PLDT vice-president for marketing George Lim said at an analysts' briefing.
PLDT has proposed to raise monthly fixed local rates and national long distance rates but lower international long distance rates and implement a call-metering scheme.
Lim said the NTC has conducted five public hearings on PLDT's rate scheme but it is yet to decide on the case. Another hearing is set for August 6.
PLDT officials earlier said the rate restructuring would help offset lower revenues from a reduction in international call rates.
PLDT has been negotiating with AT&T for a new accounting rate, or the cost of processed international calls, now at $1.00 a minute.
PLDT executive vice-president Edgardo del Fonso told analysts that a 10 cent drop in accounting rates translated to a $30 million decline in annual revenues.
